correctness.rationale: All nine adjacent pairs occur: same-letter and successor pairs appear within images, and predecessor pairs across images of a repeated letter. For the weighted recurrence split a window of length k^(m+1) into r whole blocks and two end fragments which themselves form a legal length-k^m window when joined. For attainment maintain a maximizing window starting in the first block of either (c-1,c) or (c,c+1), where c maximizes the level-m block weight. At offset j in either first block, the suffix, r copies of U_c, and the required length-j prefix occur in U_(c-1)^r U_c U_c^r U_(c+1). The lift starts in the first large block, so its new pair (c-1,c) serves for either allowed next maximizer c or c-1; c+1 cannot strictly beat c. At m=0 the invariant holds with the maximizing letter as the first block. Applying this to weights ±1_{a=0}, with the sliding-window step at most one, gives the exact complexity. The cyclic Fourier formula and its difference product yield the median criterion at m=3n, where the parity vector is (0,1,1). The rational cosine of 2 arg(r+ω) lies strictly between 1/2 and 1, so on every progression 3pn both sides of the median criterion occur infinitely often. Thus the range parity and, by differencing and odd r, complexity parity are not eventually periodic at powers. A finite automaton on the inputs 10^m would be eventually periodic, contrary to the reduction modulo 2 of any integer k-regular sequence. The supplied Python and output are finite corroboration only; the block-invariant and parity proof were reconstructed from the frozen text.
